The user wants me to reconsider the ORIGINAL source code (the original RTL provided in the first prompt) using the discovery observations provided in the second prompt. The discovery observations show that the original RTL fails CTS flow control checks in several profiles (violations like "ready_while_receiver_blocks", "byte_accepted_while_receiver_blocks", "ready_while_receiver_blocks", "byte_accepted_while_receiver_blocks").

The contract in the first prompt says:
"CTS is active low. When setup[30] is zero, a receiver that has blocked continuously for at least eight clocks must not see busy go low or a new byte accepted. CTS changes have synchronizer latency. An in-flight byte may finish."

The discovery observations show violations:
1. "ready_while_receiver_blocks" - busy goes low (ready goes high) while receiver blocks (CTS high/blocking).
2. "byte_accepted_while_receiver_blocks" - byte accepted (i_wr && !o_busy) while receiver blocks.

The contract says: "When setup[30] is zero, a receiver that has blocked continuously for at least eight clocks must not see busy go low or a new byte accepted. CTS changes have synchronizer latency. An in-flight byte may finish."

The original RTL has a CTS synchronizer: `qq_cts_n`, `q_cts_n`, `ck_cts`.
`always @(posedge i_clk) { qq_cts_n, q_cts_n } <= { q_cts_n, i_cts_n };`
`always @(posedge i_clk) ck_cts <= (!qq_cts_n)||(!hw_flow_control);`
`hw_flow_control = !r_setup[30]` (so enabled when setup[30] == 0).
`i_cts_n` is active low CTS (Ready To Send). `i_cts_n` = 1 means receiver blocks (not ready).
`qq_cts_n` is `i_cts_n` delayed by 2 cycles.
`ck_cts` = `(!qq_cts_n) || (!hw_flow_control)`.
`!qq_cts_n` means `qq_cts_n` is 0, meaning `i_cts_n` was 0 two cycles ago (receiver ready).
`!hw_flow_control` means flow control disabled (setup[30] == 1).
So `ck_cts` is 1 when receiver is ready (after 2 cycle sync) OR flow control disabled.
`ck_cts` = 1 means "clear to send" (CTS asserted).

In the IDLE state logic:
```verilog

        r_busy <= 1'b1;
        case(i_data_bits)
        ...
        endcase
    end else begin // Stay in idle
        r_busy <= !ck_cts;

end
```

So `r_busy` (which is `o_busy`) goes low (`!ck_cts`) in IDLE state when NOT writing.
`ck_cts` = `(!qq_cts_n) || (!hw_flow_control)`.
`!ck_cts` = `qq_cts_n && hw_flow_control`.

But comment says: "Hardware flow control Ready-To-Send bit. Set this to one to use the core without flow control."
